name: Fantasy console pixel
region: Online, from a single maker's tool
summary: A made-up console sets the limits: a 128×128 pixel screen, a fixed palette of 16 colours and small 8×8 sprites. Makers choose the 8-bit look as a rule of the tool, not as a limit of old hardware.

philosophy.core_thesis: If a tool fixes the limits of an imagined console, every maker shares one palette and one pixel scale, and the limits become a common style.
design_principles: Draw on a screen of 128×128 pixels and keep every shape on whole pixels.
Pick colours only from the one shared palette of 16 colours.
Build sprites and tiles from 8×8 pixel cells.
Show a whole room or a small level on one screen, or scroll a map in tile steps.
Keep the user interface in the same pixel font and the same palette as the game.

projection_and_camera.camera: Locked on one screen, or scrolls in whole tiles; top-down views are also common.
projection_and_camera.framing: A square of 16×16 tiles of 8 px; the whole play area is visible at once.

geometry.primitive: An 8×8 pixel cell; sprites of 8×8 or a multiple of it.
geometry.budget: One shared sprite sheet and one tile map; a small game holds a few hundred sprites.
geometry.edge_rule: Hard pixel steps; diagonals in clean 1:1 or 2:1 runs.
geometry.proportion: A character is 1 tile high; a door is 1 to 2 tiles; a room fills one screen.

surface.texture_rule: A material is a 2- or 3-colour pattern inside one 8×8 tile, repeated.
surface.texel_density: 1 tile of 8 px for each metre at the scale of the character
surface.filtering: Nearest neighbour; the 128 px screen is scaled by whole numbers.
surface.material_model: Painted: each material is a fixed tile with its colours in it.

palette.strategy: One shared palette of 16 colours for every game; shade by moving to the next colour of the same hue family.
palette.colour_depth: 4 bits for each pixel, from a fixed palette of 16

lighting.model: Painted into the tiles; no light engine.
lighting.shadows: A dark blue or dark purple tile under an object.
lighting.atmosphere: None, or a palette swap for fog and night.
lighting.time_of_day: A swap of the sky colour; night uses black and dark blue.

world_and_space.scale: A door is 1 to 2 tiles high for a character of 1 tile.
world_and_space.interiors: A room is one 16×16 tile screen with furniture as single sprites.
world_and_space.exteriors: A level is a row of screens or a scrolled tile map under a flat sky colour.
world_and_space.threshold: Walk off the screen edge or into a door and cut to the next screen.

principles.rule: Draw a door 2 tiles high for a character of 1 tile.
Use 2 planes: a tile map and sprites in front.
Keep the player in the middle third of the 128 px screen.

interface.placement: Text and counters in the corners of the 128×128 screen, about 8% of the height.
interface.type_and_icons: A small built-in pixel font; icons are single 8×8 sprites in the shared palette.
interface.diegesis: Mostly on top; the user interface of the tool uses the same palette.

emotion.target_response: Warm nostalgia with a maker's pride: the viewer sees a small, complete world made within strict limits.

avoid_when: The brief needs more than 16 colours or a high-resolution screen.

modifiers.how: Widen the palette to 256 colours on a 256×224 screen with parallax layers.
Drop the pixel grid; use flat pastel faces in an isometric view.

render_resolution.note: The console screen is 128 px; the 144 px floor of the domain range is used for the framed display.

colour_depth.note: 16 fixed colours; 5 bits only with the 16 extra palette colours.
